_doc: Extra store-ops parameters that sim/ops.py needs but data/ops/params.json does not cover. Same shape: value, unit, source ('assumption: <why>' when unsourced), confidence. Every one here is LOW confidence unless it points at a file in this repo. Edit a value and re-run; the day file records which value was used.

open_hours.source: assumption: typical UK large-supermarket weekday hours 08:00-22:00 (task spec)

walk_speed_mps.source: sim/layout_optimise.py PARAMS.walk_speed_mps = web/src/layout.ts G.walkSpeed (assumption: in-store walking slower than ~1.4 m/s street pace)

staff_walk_speed_mps.source: assumption: staff walk at shopper pace pushing a cage/mop bucket

browse_dwell_slots.unit: rows scanned on an off-mission unit
browse_dwell_slots.source: assumption: a browsing shopper glances at one row (time = 1 x seconds_at_shelf) instead of all 4

mission_categories_xl.source: sim/run.py MISSION_CATEGORIES (assumption) extended to the 4 XL categories: bread/hot drinks/frozen on the weekly shop, bread on top-up, sweets + ice cream (desserts) on the treat mission (assumption)

in_range_share_of_basket.unit: share of the mission basket that comes from the 12 modelled categories
in_range_share_of_basket.source: assumption: the 12 modelled categories are ambient/chilled grocery only (no fresh produce, meat, household, alcohol); a weekly trolley draws well under half from them. The rest are 'off-range' items: they count at the till but not on our shelves

basket_nb_dispersion_k.source: assumption: right-skewed basket counts (params.json basket_size_distribution); k=4 gives CV ~0.5 at mean 40

loose_produce_share_of_offrange.unit: share of off-range items that are loose produce needing weighing
loose_produce_share_of_offrange.source: assumption: loose fruit/veg lines in a trolley; no UK figure fetched

age_restricted_basket_prob.unit: P(basket holds an age-restricted item: alcohol, paracetamol, energy drinks)
age_restricted_basket_prob.source: assumption: not sourced; drives age_check_delay_s_* only

service_time_cv.unit: lognormal CV on the formula service time
service_time_cv.source: assumption: Klee 2006 reports means/regressions only; a 30% CV keeps the queue stochastic without changing the mean

patience_min.unit: mean minutes a shopper will stand in a queue before abandoning (gamma, shape patience_gamma_shape)
patience_min.source: assumption: no grocery reneging data fetched; bigger baskets have more sunk effort so wait longer

card_only_payment.source: assumption: everyone pays by card (Klee debit intercept + WPI card payment); cash tender times in params.json are not used

sco_accept_fallback.source: assumption: used only when Jev is off (--no-jev) or the call cap is hit; the default path asks Jev

basket_buckets.source: assumption: word buckets handed to Jev (numbers as words, jaggedness #2)

bump_k_per_other.unit: P(bump) = 1-exp(-k * others in the same aisle segment) per unit visit
bump_k_per_other.source: assumption: links collisions to crowding; a 4 m walkway x 6.4 m unit holds ~6 people before contact is likely

spill_detour_m.unit: metres added when a shopper turns back from a blocked aisle
spill_detour_m.source: assumption: back out of the walkway and come in from the other end = 2 x unit length (6.4 m)

restock_case_units.source: assumption: typical ambient/chilled outer case of 6-24

restock_smart_pso_threshold.source: assumption: the priority policy also restocks a SKU above the 25% trigger when its stock-out risk before the next round exceeds 30%

margin_proxy_by_role.unit: gross-margin share used only to rank restock tasks
margin_proxy_by_role.source: assumption: own label carries the retailer's highest margin; not sourced. Margin is only a tie-break weight in the priority score

backroom_cover_days.unit: initial backroom stock in days of forecast demand (uniform per SKU, hashed draw)
backroom_cover_days.source: assumption: Reiner et al. 2013 report dairy dwells 12.5 h in the back room (about half a day); ambient cover varies. A uniform spread makes some SKUs short on day 1, which is what the manager is for

delivery_hour.source: Reiner, Teller & Kotzab 2013 (see params.json lead_time_days_chilled): their simulation delivers at 6 a.m.

manager_review_min.source: assumption: hourly review during trading (params.json order_review_period_days = 1 is the supplier cut; the manager checks more often and orders as soon as IP <= ROP)

forecast_shoppers_per_mission.source: assumption: the manager's 'history' = a Monte Carlo of the same shopper model (separate seed namespace), giving E[units per shopper] by product and mission

surrogate_shrinkage_m.source: assumption: empirical-Bayes shrinkage of each (archetype, product) P(take|noticed) toward the archetype mean, (k + m*p_arch)/(n + m)

menu.name: All Butter Croissant (Tesco Finest, served singly)
Plant Chef falafel and houmous sandwich (Tesco)

cafe.source: assumption: seat count, visit shares (more mid-morning/afternoon per the idea doc), 20 min dwell, 3 min max wait for a seat, and all menu prices are unsourced; menu items are real OFF products (codes from data/products/uk_products.parquet). Not in store_xl.config.json (that file is owned elsewhere), so the cafe sits between the entrances and the aisle block here

theft.source: assumption: BRC Crime Survey 2025/26 and ONS shoplifting figures were not fetched (web search budget spent), so the attempt share (0.4% of trips), tag share, EAS detection rate, guard speed and the 25 s window in which a guard can stop the shopper at the gate are all labelled assumptions

night_fill.source: assumption: a night crew refills every shelf from the back room before opening (common UK supermarket practice, not sourced); only back-room stock can be used, so a SKU with an empty back room opens short

offrange_item_price_gbp.source: assumption: an off-range item is valued at the mean price of the 480-SKU catalog (computed at run time); only used for the value of abandoned baskets

shelf_capacity_multiplier.source: assumption: planogram_xl.json capacity = facings x ONE layer of depth (store_xl.config.json stock_rules); real shelves stack most packs 2+ high. At x1 the 3,369-unit store holds ~1/5 of a Saturday's modelled demand on these 480 SKUs; run --set shelf_capacity_multiplier=1 to see that case

restock_batch_fill_below.source: assumption: once at a unit with the cage, a restocker also tops up any other SKU on the same unit below 50% full (working the bay, both policies)

patience_gamma_shape.source: assumption: an exponential patience (k=1, the Erlang-A default) makes ~1 in 4 meal-deal shoppers quit after 2 min, which is not what UK tills look like; k=3 keeps impatience but thins that tail. No grocery reneging data fetched
